business_problem: Skild AI needed a way to train robots that can adapt across many bodies, tasks, and environments, but collecting enough real-world robotics data was too slow and expensive to produce robust general-purpose physical AI.
solution_summary: Skild AI built the Skild Brain as an omni-bodied robot foundation model on NVIDIA accelerated computing and simulation tools so it could train physical AI without depending on massive real-world robot fleets. The company uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA Isaac Lab to create large-scale physics simulations across thousands of robot embodiments and environments, while NVIDIA Cosmos Transfer augments those datasets with varied lighting and visual conditions. This synthetic pipeline is paired with human videos from the internet to teach robots how objects afford actions, giving the model broader behavioral coverage than teleoperation data alone. In deployment, the Skild Brain consumes raw camera images and proprioceptive signals and directly outputs low-level motor commands, enabling zero- or minimal-post-training adaptation to new robots. The result is a robotics stack that learns through scalable simulation and data augmentation rather than narrowly programmed behaviors.

solution_components.name: Skild Brain
solution_components.role: Acts as the omni-bodied robot foundation model that drives decision-making and motor control across robot types.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Omniverse
solution_components.role: Provides simulation libraries used to generate large-scale synthetic robotics data.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Isaac Lab
solution_components.role: Creates the physics-based simulation scenarios used for reinforcement-learning training at scale.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Cosmos Transfer
solution_components.role: Augments training datasets with diverse visual and environmental variations to improve robustness.

data_flow: Synthetic robot scenarios and internet-scale human videos are fed into Skild AI's training pipeline, Isaac Lab and Omniverse generate scalable simulation experience, Cosmos Transfer augments the data, and the resulting Skild Brain turns vision and proprioception into low-level motor commands for new robot bodies in real-world tasks.
business_outcome: Skild AI achieved 60-80 percent task performance within hours of data collection, enabled robots to carry payloads up to 1.5x body weight, reduced total cost of ownership by 10x compared with traditional systems, and demonstrated recovery from jams and limb failures through in-context adaptation rather than reprogramming.
